title: Playing drums for Shaw: rhythm section struggles and the tom-tom
summary: Leeman struggles to make Shaw's rhythm section swing like Basie and uses a small Chinese tom-tom behind Shaw's choruses, an idea from Goodman's 'Sing, Sing, Sing'.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: I was trying to develop my style of drumming, but I had to coincide with the type of music that we
played, with the type of band that we were developing -- so it was a little rough with Artie Shaw's temperament, and you wait here and I'll explain. But stop it for a minute.

: I'm in the same vintage as you, and you are considered during the big band era, the epitome of jazz, of a big band jazz drummer. The things that you set were the standards which Buddy Rich followed, which Dave Tough followed, which Cozy Cole followed, which all of the great big band jazz drummers followed. Now you were going to tell me -- you said that when you were with Charlie Barnet, you were trying to establish your own style, so continue with that.

Let's stay with Shaw. I was grateful to Shaw for the opportunities he gave me, as a kid learning. The rhythm section was a struggle for me -- I never came out in any of the records we made, they were all hits, they did such great things, but it was a struggle for me. Sid Weiss was a good bass player, and Al Avola worked real well with me -- he was the guitar player. The band was really swinging, and I was trying to get them to swing like Basie, and it didn't work out. I had a little problem with the piano player keeping time. But those are the things that you overcome.
A drummer might be interested in this, because one reason I wanted to play on the top cymbal [with Artie] on clarinet, I
always felt that way, you know? And Artie Shaw wanted -- the tom toms came in to prominence with Benny Goodman when he made that 'Sing, Sing, Sing'.

So Shaw thought that he would keep the tom tom idea behind his chorus, but he wanted it behind all his choruses -- and all these great records we made, you listen. So I had a special little tom tom, a little Chinese tom tom, and I worked it and I stuffed it up with bandaids; God knows what else.
